summary: Clean loop with no pops, but it reads as a held 'hands up' pose that breathes rather than a fall: every bone is keyed on 0/12/24 and the arms only move 12-15 deg. Fixes: turn the arm motion into a real circular flail, stagger forearms, shins, feet and head, and add a counter-twist through the torso. The blend from jump is fine (similar leg tuck, arms already raised).

findings.observation: The spec asks for arms 'waving for balance', but on the sheets F000 and F012 are almost the same silhouette and the onion skin shows a single arm shape. UpperArm.rz moves only 15 deg (left) and 12 deg (right), UpperArm.rx is a flat -10, so the hands travel on a short straight line in one plane. The arm amplitude is doubled and an out-of-phase forward/back swing is added on rx (left forward at 6, back at 18; right the opposite), which makes each hand trace a loop instead of a line.

metrics: overlap_score 0.0, 11 of 13 bones keyed on frame 12, and whole-body speed drops to 2.5 deg/frame on frames 0, 11, 12 and 23, so the whole body stops and reverses together twice per loop. Both feet are frozen (Foot.rx range 0). Forearms are delayed 3 frames, shins 2, head 3, and the feet get a loose dangle on different frames, so no frame has everything at rest.

The trunk is a rigid column: LowerTorso.rx moves 2 deg and UpperTorso.rx 3 deg, with no twist, so the flailing arms do not act on the body (side view F000-F024, the teal blocks never move). A chest counter-twist (ry -7 at 6, +7 at 18, against the arm that swings forward) and double the rock on rx are added.
